ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals of square $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. $E$ is any point on $BC$, $EG \perp BD$ at point $G$, and $EF \perp AC$ at point $F$. If $AC=10$, what is the value of $EG+EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle OBC = \angle OCB = 45^\circ$, AC$\perp$BD, and OC=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=5,\\
$\because EG \perp$BD and EF$\perp$AC,\\
$\therefore quadrilateral EFOG is a rectangle, and \triangle BEG$, $\triangle CEF$ are isosceles right triangles,\\
$\therefore EG=FO, CF=EF,\\
\therefore EG+EF=FO+CF=CO=\boxed{5}$
